title: Swim Star Tatjana Smith Changes Teams
summary: Tatjana Smith is South Africa's most decorated Olympian. Now she will swim for the Netherlands. Smith won four Olympic medals in breaststroke, including two golds, before she retired after the Paris 2024 Games. She came back to swimming in September. She hopes to race in the 50m breaststroke at the 2028 Games in Los Angeles, when the event is held for the first time at the Olympics. Smith has dual citizenship because her father is Dutch. She said she has 'always been Dutch and South African.' She also said the move gives her more support and a better chance to build a lasting career. Money worries had helped push her to stop swimming before. 'Representing South Africa was a childhood dream come true,' she said. 'But dreams can change as we grow.' Smith will keep living and training in South Africa. She will first swim for the Netherlands at the short course World Championships from December 1 to 6. She knows the switch may disappoint some fans. South Africa's sports ministry said, 'South Africa does not own her.'
why_it_matters: Athletes get to choose their own path, and seeing someone chase a dream in a new place shows that changing your mind is part of growing up.
